A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSG-12M dataset and Poly2Graph pipeline. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and matchable despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original GNN classification experiments in Table 2 and GPU memory and throughput measurements in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 reports expanded original classification experiments, resource measurements, and a Poly2Graph timing comparison in Appendix C.5.

M1.justification: The reference GNN input representation changes from 13-dimensional edge features containing five sampled coordinate pairs to six-dimensional summaries containing length, endpoint distance, midpoint, and average potential/DOS. Poly2Graph's extraction procedure and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on balanced HSG-three-band and full HSG-12M. This extends testing to higher-band geometric variations beyond the topology-deduplicated population evaluated in v1, although HSG-topology already represented all 1401 classes. Dataset construction and sizes remain unchanged, and neither version evaluates temporal tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands from GCN, GIN, GAT, and GraphSAGE to eight comparators by adding GATv2, GINE, Molecular Fingerprints, and CGCNN. These additions participate in comparisons on the original three subsets as well as the newly evaluated subsets.

E3.justification: V1's five-epoch runs become runs capped at 100 epochs and 1000 steps. Batch sizes change from 256/64 to 6000, dropout from 0.1 to zero, and initial learning rate from 0.01 to 0.001. V2 introduces model-specific widths targeting parameter counts within 4%, two-GPU DDP, revised edge preprocessing, and Top-5/test-loss evaluation. The 80/10/10 stratified split ratio is retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C.5 adds an analysis of computation time as polynomial degree range increases from two to six; v1 provided only aggregate speed claims. The fragmentation gallery and extraction-quality checks are retained. The additional classification tables do not introduce a separate controlled ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report classification means and standard deviations over three seeds, but seed identities change from 42/624/706 to 42/2025/666. V2 additionally reports standard deviations for throughput and GPU memory, whereas v1 reported averages only. There is no documented increase in classification run count.

E6.justification: Classification and resource results are extensively replaced under revised settings. For example, GraphSAGE one-band accuracy changes from 0.694±0.010 to 0.854±0.003; this is not a same-setting improvement. V2 adds full-dataset results, test loss, Top-5 accuracy, and timing measurements showing approximately 120,000–230,000-fold spectral-potential speedups. GraphSAGE retains the best Top-1 and Macro-F1 ranking.

T1.justification: V2 replaces the binary z-support definition of polynomial classes with bivariate monomial support modulo parity. Appendix B also revises multiband matrix dimensions and Hermiticity conditions, distinguishes hopping range from determinant degree, and adds degree bounds and examples. Appendix F newly asserts that a smallest graph multiset gives a canonical signature, without establishing uniqueness.

C1.justification: The central dataset, automation, spatial-multigraph novelty, and algebra-to-graph universality claims remain. The quantitative efficiency claim is narrowed from v1's million-fold speedup and 20–40-fold memory advantage to approximately hundred-thousand-fold speedup without a fixed memory-improvement factor.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantial interpretations concerning edge-feature utility, attention overhead, parameter efficiency, and Top-k retrieval for inverse design. Appendix H explicitly discusses information lost by the reference edge summaries and narrows the claimed practical relevance of fragmentation. Some interpretations overreach: the claimed consistent GINE superiority contradicts one-band accuracy in Table 2, where GIN scores 0.799 versus GINE's 0.764.

D1.justification: Appendix E substantially expands implementation documentation with per-model widths, activation and attention-head settings, and distributed-training configuration. V2 newly describes an auxiliary HSG-12M package supporting reproduction and custom featurization. Existing access locations and most Poly2Graph tutorial content are retained, but the explicit Python-version requirement is removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations supporting the four additional baselines and a related graph-transformer study, while pruning background citations including GOOD, PowerGraph, and The Well. The substantive positioning against existing spatial and multigraph resources remains largely intact; relocating Related Work is principally organizational.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially reorganized around physical-science motivation and automated extraction, and the contributions are reordered. Related Work moves to Appendix A, the mathematical and benchmark material gains extensive subsection structure, and limitations move into an expanded Appendix H. An appendix contents list and reproducibility, ethics, and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: Table 2 is transposed and expanded, and the appendices add timing, conceptual-summary, feature, configuration, test-loss, and Top-5 tables while separating throughput and memory displays. The document template and figure placement change throughout. The tutorial plots are retained as unnumbered inline images rather than deleted; the underlying raster images match across versions.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's explicitly minimal validation by evaluating the balanced higher-band and full datasets, adding edge-aware comparators and parameter-count controls, and supplying direct extraction-timing evidence. Revised class definitions and expanded implementation documentation improve assessability and reproducibility. New interpretive overstatements and the unproved canonical-signature assertion are weaknesses, but the stronger empirical foundation provides a substantial net improvement.
